note: Named traditions of typeset running text, for authoring read-mode worlds. It exists because a 54-world audit of the read pool found the pool could serve reading but was built almost entirely from traditions of display, and because the two ways a read world fails pull against each other. A world can be unreadable, where the tradition has only a display voice so body copy inherits poster lettering and arrives as four paragraphs of all caps. Or it can be generic, perfectly readable and something a model produces unprompted, which is what happened to every entry mined from contemporary web practice. Clearing both at once is what makes read the hardest of the four modes, and what these traditions are chosen for: each one is specific enough and dated enough to be distinctive, and each one had running text as its actual job, so it already contains a body face.
rule: The reviewer's criterion, from the audit: a world can serve read only if its system contains a body face and not only a display voice. A tradition whose artifacts carry no paragraph of running text cannot supply one.

axes.label: The read surface to design
axes.note: Read is not one thing either. The wave pipeline previously drew only documentation surfaces, which is part of why it produced only documentation-shaped worlds.
